note: The open-internet survey named anthropics/claude-code-security-review (MIT, Anthropic-authored) as a clean, on-target way to put a diff-aware security review over the crypto-seal and ledger code that Nestor's own tests cannot fully cover from outside. Wired as .github/workflows/security-review.yml -- advisory, not part of the required test gate, and a no-op without the API key.

decisions.question: How is the security-review action wired so it helps without breaking CI for forks and un-configured checkouts?
decisions.commitment: A separate workflow (security-review.yml) on pull_request, NOT wired into the required 'test' aggregate gate, so it advises and never blocks a merge. A first step checks whether secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and gates the checkout + review steps on it; without the key the job prints a ::notice:: and succeeds, so fork PRs and key-less checkouts stay green. Permissions are the minimum the action needs (contents: read, pull-requests: write). docs/dogfood and bench/results are excluded from the scan as derived artifacts.
decisions.why: A required gate that hard-fails whenever a secret is absent would break every fork PR and every contributor who hasn't set the key -- the action's claude-api-key input is required, and fork PRs can't read secrets at all. Making it advisory and self-skipping keeps it useful where configured and invisible where not, matching the repo's fail-loud-not-break posture. It is separate from the unit gate because a security opinion from a model is signal for a human, not a merge blocker.

decisions.question: The action publishes no release tags. Pin it how?
decisions.commitment: Referenced at @main, with a comment in the workflow stating the residual risk and that it should be pinned to a reviewed commit SHA once one is chosen. actions/checkout is pinned at @v7 to match the existing tests.yml rather than introduce a second version.
decisions.why: A moving ref on a third-party action is a supply-chain risk -- the exact class this review exists to catch -- so pretending @main is pinned would be dishonest. There is no tag to pin to yet, and pinning to an arbitrary current SHA without review only trusts @main at a point in time; naming the risk in the file is the honest state until a maintainer reviews and pins a SHA.
